Vnde postea versu 14. sessionis huius ad dexteram Dei rationem reddit ex eo quod vnica sui oblatione suos sanctificarit.
units.tr: 12 But this one) The apodosis of the dissimilarity, which is the assumption of the syllogism. Sat down at the right hand) The proper dissimilarity required that it be said that Christ, offered once as a victim for sins and abiding for ever, sanctifies us. But for sanctification he could put the session of Christ at the right hand of the Father, which follows upon our sanctification and necessarily presupposes it as preceding. For Christ then first began to sit at the right hand of God, and attained his glory, when, having once offered his victim, he had sanctified and perfected his people. Whence afterwards, in verse 14, he gives the reason for this sitting at the right hand of God, namely that by one offering of himself he has sanctified his people.

units.la: 13 Id quod superest)Hæc verba innuunt nondum esse perfectam & completam Christi, etiam sedentis ad dexteram Patris, gloriam. Nam Christus ad dexteram Patris sedens, expectat donec inimici ipsius scabellum pedum eius fiant. Confer hunc locum cum eo qui est 1.Corinth.15. 24.25. 26. Consecrauit in) Sensus est: Perfecit atque absoluit eos, qui sanctificantur: quo significat perfectionem hanc positam in sanctificatione.
units.tr: 13 What remains) These words imply that the glory of Christ, even as he sits at the right hand of the Father, is not yet perfect and complete. For Christ, sitting at the right hand of the Father, waits until his enemies are made the footstool of his feet. Compare this passage with 1 Corinthians 15:24, 25, 26. He has perfected) The sense is: he has perfected and completed those who are sanctified; by which he signifies that this perfection consists in sanctification.

units.la: 15 Testificatur autem)Sequitur argumentum tertium, quo ostendit Christi oblationem illam semel factam sufficere. Argumentum est ab efsecto illius oblationis, peccatorum remissione & oblatione, quæ pars quædam est perfectionis, qua pro argumento usus est proxime. Nam persectionis nomen (ut mihi videtur) comprehendit in se omnia simul beneficia, quæ Christus morte sua nobis promeritus est, in quibus censetur peccatorum remissio. Syllogismus est. Vbi est peccatorum remissio, non est amplius oblatio pro peccato. Atqui ex unica Christi oblatione est peccatorum remissio. Ergo non est amplius oblatio Christi, sive sufficit unica illa oblatio. Assumptionem confirmat testimonio Spiritus sancti loquentis Ierem. 31. 33. Primum præfatur Spiritum sanctum hoc nobis testificari. Deinde testimonium Spiritus in medium adducit, in quo testimonio promissio facta est remissionis peccatorum omnium. Peccatorum ista remissio promissa intelligenda est futura in sanguine Christi, qui novi fœderis Mediator est. Vide quæ de hoc testimonio diximus supra cap. 8. vers. 8 & deinceps 18 Porro ubi) Syllogismi propositio.
units.tr: 15 Moreover the Holy Spirit testifies) There follows the third argument, by which he shows that that offering of Christ, made once, is sufficient. The argument is from the effect of that offering, the remission of sins and the offering, which is a part of perfection, which he used as an argument just before. For the name of perfection (as it seems to me) embraces all the benefits which Christ merited for us by his death, among which the remission of sins is reckoned. It is a syllogism: where there is remission of sins, there is no longer an offering for sin. But by the one offering of Christ there is remission of sins. Therefore there is no longer an offering for sin, or that one offering of Christ is sufficient. He confirms the assumption with the testimony of the Holy Spirit speaking in Jeremiah 31:33. First he states that the Holy Spirit testifies this to us. Then he brings forward the testimony of the Spirit, in which a promise of the remission of all sins is made. This promised remission of sins is to be understood as future, in the blood of Christ, who is the Mediator of the new covenant. See what we said about this testimony above, chapter 8, verse 8 and following. 18 Now where) The proposition of the syllogism.

units.la: 19 Quum igitur, fratres, habeamus libertatem ingrediendi Sacrarium per sanguinem Iesu,
units.tr: 19 Since therefore, brethren, we have liberty to enter into the sanctuary by the blood of Jesus,

units.la: 20 Eam viam quam dedicavit nobis recentem & viventem per velum, hoc est, per carnem suam:
units.tr: 20 By the way which he has consecrated for us, new and living, through the veil, that is, through his flesh:

units.la: 21 Quumque habeamus Sacerdotem magnum, præfectum domui Dei. 22 Accedamus cum vero corde, & certa persuasione fidei, puris cordibus à conscientia mala.
units.tr: 21 And since we have a great priest, set over the house of God. 22 Let us draw near with a true heart and with a certain assurance of faith, with hearts pure from an evil conscience.

units.la: 23 Et abluto corpore aqua pura, teneamus consessionem spei non vacillantem: ) fidelis enim est qui promisit.)
units.tr: 23 And having our body washed with pure water, let us hold fast the confession of hope without wavering: (for he is faithful who promised.)

units.la: 24 Et obseruemus alij alios, ut nos acuamus ad charitatem & bona opera.
units.tr: 24 And let us consider one another, so as to stir up one another to love and good works.

units.la: 25 Non deserentes aggregationem nostri mutuam, sicuti mos est quibusdam, sed adhortantes alij alios, idque eo magis quod videtis illum diem appropinquare.
units.tr: 25 Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as is the custom of some, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the day drawing near.

units.la: Quum igitur, fratres, )Haētenus de Pontificatu Christi, inde à principio capitis ad hunc usque locum. Nunc redit ad institutam exhortationem, qua ad perseuerantiam in fide adhortatur. Hic itaque habemus exhortationis argumentum nonum, quod sumptum est à libertate ingrediendi sacrarium cœleste: in hanc formam. Quam habemus libertatem ingrediendi sacrarium, accedamus cum vero corde &c. At habemus libertatem ingrediendi sacrarium. Ergo accedamus. Persanguinem) Libertatem hanc ingrediendi sacrarium explicat, ex caussa efficiente meritoria, siue pretio quo redempta est; nempe Christi sanguine.
units.tr: Since therefore, brethren,) Hitherto concerning the priesthood of Christ, from the beginning of the chapter to this point. Now he returns to the exhortation he began, by which he urges perseverance in the faith. Here, then, we have the ninth argument of exhortation, which is taken from the liberty to enter the heavenly sanctuary, in this form: We have the liberty to enter the sanctuary; let us draw near with a true heart, etc. But we have liberty to enter the sanctuary. Therefore let us draw near. By the blood) He explains this liberty to enter the sanctuary from its efficient and meritorious cause, or the price by which it was redeemed, namely the blood of Christ.

units.la: 20 Εὰ Υἱα) Libertatem ingrediendi explicat deinde à via per quam ingredimur Sacrarium cœleste. Viam hanc describit, primùm ex eo quod dedicata sit à Christo & consecrata. Deinde ex eo quod recens sit. Tertiò ex eo quod viua fit. Quarto viam ipsam exprelse nominat, vocatque velum, h.e.vt ipse exponit carnem Christi,quam velum vocat per allusionem ad velum quod praetendebatur Arcae Dei,quae collocabatur in Sancto sanctorum. Sic enim naturae humanae velum praetenditur Deitati Christi,cuius typus erat arca foederis.
units.tr: 20 [ἣν ἐνεκαίνισεν] ) He then explains the liberty of entering from the way by which we enter the heavenly sanctuary. He describes this way, first from the fact that it was dedicated and consecrated by Christ. Second, from the fact that it is new. Third, from the fact that it is living. Fourth, he names the way itself expressly and calls it a veil, that is, as he himself explains, the flesh of Christ, which he calls a veil by allusion to the veil which was stretched before the Ark of God, which was placed in the Holy of Holies. For thus the veil of human nature is stretched before the Deity of Christ, of which the ark of the covenant was a type.

units.la: 21 Quumque habeamus)Hoc exhortationis argumentum est decimum, a praefecto domus Dei, sive sacrarij in quod ingrediendum est. Is autem est idem ille Pontifex magnus, de quo hactenus.Cum igitur & aditus pateat ad sacrarium coeleste, & Pontifex noster sit praefectus domui Dei,sive sacrario,quid vetat quo minus ingrediamur & accedamus? De Christi praefectura in domo Dei, vide supra 6.3. At Christus vt Filius domui suae praeest.
units.tr: 21 And since we have) This is the tenth argument of exhortation, taken from the one set over the house of God, or the sanctuary into which we are to enter. He is that same great High Priest of whom we have spoken so far. Since, therefore, both the way to the heavenly sanctuary lies open and our High Priest is set over the house of God, or the sanctuary, what forbids us from entering and drawing near? On the rule of Christ over the house of God, see above, 3:6. For Christ, as the Son, rules over his own house.

units.la: 22 Accedamus)Haec altera est pars propositionis consequentiae,quae incepta est a verf.19. Continet autem plures in se partes, sive membra plura,quorum primum habetur hoc versu. Est autem opus fidei, quod cernitur in accedendo ad sacrarium, sive in ingrediendo Sacrarium coeleste. In accedendo tria requirit. Primum cor verum, h. e. sinceritatem cordis, quod Paulus cor purum vocat. 1. Timoth. 1. 5. Secundum est πληροφορία fidei,quam eodem sensu illo loco Paulus fidem ἀνυπόκριτον appellat. Tertium est purificatio cordium a conscientia mala,quam Paulus illo loco bonam conscientiam tiam fiam nuncupat.His igitur tribus modis oportet affectum esse ejus animum, qui accedit ad fa-crarium illud coeleste.
units.tr: 22 Let us draw near) This is the second part of the proposition of the consequence, which began at verse 19. It contains several parts, or several members, of which the first is found in this verse. Now it is a work of faith, which is seen in drawing near to the sanctuary, or in entering the heavenly sanctuary. In drawing near it requires three things. First, a true heart, that is, sincerity of heart, which Paul calls a pure heart, 1 Timothy 1:5. Second is the full assurance of faith [πληροφορία πίστεως], which in the same sense Paul in that place calls faith unfeigned [ἀνυπόκριτος]. Third is the purification of hearts from an evil conscience, which Paul in that place calls a good conscience. Thus the disposition of the mind of him who draws near to that heavenly sanctuary ought to be affected in these three ways.

units.la: 25 Et abluto corpore ) Secundum membrum est posterioris partis propositionis consequentiæ, de qua diximus. Est autem perseverantia in opere spei. Opus spei est confessio non vacillans, h.e. constans confessio quæ spei tribuitur, quia spes vitæ æternæ facit ut confiteamur Christum coram mundo. Gloriamur sub spe gloriæ Dei. Rom. 5. 2. In tenenda confessione spei requirit corpus ablutum aqua pura, h.e. sanctificationem hominis, quam adumbrat per legales & externas ablutiones sordium corporis. Aquam puram intelligit Spiritum Dei sanctum, cujus typus quidem erat aqua illa legalis, & cujus symbolum est aqua Sacramenti Baptismi. Fidelis enim ) Rationem perseverantiæ in confessione spei inserit, a natura, hoc est, veritate sive fidelitate Dei promittentis. Deus qui promisit natura sua verax est & immutabilis. Ergo perseveremus in confessione spei gloriæ illius quam promisit Deus.
units.tr: 25 And having our body washed) The second member of the latter part of the proposition of the consequence, of which we have spoken. It is perseverance in the work of hope. The work of hope is the unwavering confession, that is, the steadfast confession which is attributed to hope, because the hope of eternal life makes us confess Christ before the world. We glory in the hope of the glory of God, Romans 5:2. In holding fast the confession of hope he requires a body washed with pure water, that is, the sanctification of man, which he foreshadows by the legal and external washings of bodily filth. By pure water he means the Holy Spirit of God, of which that legal water was indeed a type, and of which the water of the sacrament of Baptism is the symbol. For he is faithful) He inserts the reason for perseverance in the confession of hope, taken from the nature, that is, the truth or faithfulness of God who promised. God who promised is by his nature true and unchangeable. Therefore let us persevere in the confession of the hope of that glory which God promised.

units.la: 24 Et observemus ) Hoc tertium est membrum propositionis, est autem charitatis opus positum in observatione nostri mutua. Ut nos acuamus ) Observationem quam dixit, in eo ponit, ut alij alios vicissim acuamus ad charitatem, & charitatis opus.
units.tr: 24 And let us consider) This is the third member of the proposition, and it is a work of love placed in our mutual consideration of one another. That we may stir up) He places the consideration which he mentioned in this: that we mutually stir up one another to love, and to the work of love.

units.la: 25 Non deferentes) Quartum est propositionis membrum, ad quod quarto loco adhortatur. Cõtinet exercitium pieratis, quod cernitur in celebrandis sacris coetibus & coïtionibus Sanctorum, quas hic ἐπισυναγωγὰς nomine intelligit. Primum dehortatur a desertione Ecclesiasticorum coetuum: deinde adhortatur ad eorum celebrationem, quam intelligit, cum dicit adhortantes alij alios, h. e. in vnum coeuntes, vt adhortationes, instructiones, consolationes, & caetera hujusmodi officii, in Ecclesia Dei habeantur. Sicuti) Obiter reprehendit nonnullos, qui coetus sacros non frequentabant. Idque eo magis) Exhortationis hujus argumentum, a propinquitate vltimi illius diei, cujus testem appellat ipsorum conscientiam (videtis) inquit, h.e. hujus rei ipsi estis conscij
units.tr: 25 Not forsaking) This is the fourth member of the proposition, to which he exhorts in fourth place. It contains the practice of piety, which is seen in the celebration of the holy assemblies and gatherings of the saints, which he here understands by the name gatherings [ἐπισυναγωγάς]. First he dissuades them from abandoning the ecclesiastical assemblies; then he exhorts them to celebrate these, which he understands when he says "exhorting one another", that is, coming together as one, so that exhortations, instructions, consolations and other such duties of office may be maintained in the Church of God. As is the custom) In passing he rebukes some who did not attend the holy assemblies. And all the more so) The argument for this exhortation is drawn from the nearness of that last day, of which he calls their own conscience the witness: "you see", he says, that is, you yourselves are aware of this matter.

units.la: 26 Nam si ὑλτροπεccαuerimus post acceptam cognitionem Ἀεritatis, non adhuc pro peccatis reliqua est hostia.
units.tr: 26 For if we sin wilfully [ἑκουσίως ἁμαρτανόντων] after receiving the knowledge of the truth [ἀληθείας], there remains no longer a sacrifice for sins.

units.la: 27 Sed horrenda quaedam expectatio iudicij, & ignis feruor, qui deuoraturus est aduersarios.
units.tr: 27 But a certain dreadful expectation of judgment, and a fervour of fire, which is about to devour the adversaries.

units.la: 28 Qui contempserit Mosis Legem absque misericordia ex duorum aut trium testimonio moritur.
units.tr: 28 He who has set aside the Law of Moses dies without mercy, on the testimony of two or three witnesses.

units.la: 29 Quanto (putatis) acerbiore supplicio dignus censebitur qui Filium Dei conculcarit, & sanguinem fœderis, per quem fuerat sanctificatus, profanum duxerit, & Spiritum gratiæ contumelia affecerit?
units.tr: 29 How much sharper a punishment, do you think, will be deemed due to him who has trampled underfoot the Son of God, and has counted profane the blood of the covenant by which he was sanctified, and has insulted the Spirit of grace?

units.la: 30 Nouimus enim eum qui dixit, Meum est ) lcijci, ego rependam, dicit Dominus. Et rursum, Dominus iudicabit populum suum.
units.tr: 30 For we know him who said, "Mine is ) vengeance, I will repay," says the Lord. And again, the Lord will judge his people.

units.la: 31 Horrendum est incidere in manus Dei viui.
units.tr: 31 It is a dreadful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

units.la: Non fi ) ltro) Argumentum superiorum exhortationum, a poena Apostasiae & defectionis: quasi dicat, si non perstiterimus in fide, in spe, in charitate &c. sed post acceptam veritatis cognitionem vltro peccauerimus, non adhuc &c. Vltro peccauerimus) His verbis habetur descriptio quaedam Apostasiae, siue defectionis, siue peccati in Spiritum sanctum. Primum est peccatum, deinde est peccatum in veritatem ipsam, h. e. in Euangelium Christi: Nam qui peccat in Spiritum sanctum, oppugnat ipsum Euangelium. Tertio est peccatum in veritatem Euangelij agnitam: Nam qui peccat in Spiritum sanctum, non ex ignorantia, sed ex scientia, & contra conscientiam suam peccat. Quarto peccatum est quod vltro admittitur, & sponte, hoc est, ex malitioso animi propósito. Nam qui peccat in Spiritum sanctum non ex infirmitate peccat, sed ex malitia & pertinacia animi. Post acceptam) hoc est, postquam semel fuerit illuminatus, gustaueritque donum coelestè. Heb. 6. 4. & deinceps. Non adhuc) id est, nullum est sacrificium reliquum, quo expietur ejus peccatum: quod si enim esset, illud esset vel Christi sacrificium, vel alterius cujusdam noui Mediatoris. Sed Christi sacrificium non est: nam postquàm semel admissum est hoc peccatum, quod vocatur in Spiritum sanctum,quo conculcatur Dei Filius, profanatur sanguis foederis, & Spiritus gratiæ contumelia afficitur. Iam Christi sacrificium ad eum qui sic peccauit, non amplius pertinet, & qui sic peccauit, amittit prorsus jus omne in Christi sacrificium. Ergo non est Christi sacrificium quo expiatur hujusmodi peccatum. Non est alterius cujusquam noui Mediatoris sacrificium, quo expiatur hoc peccatum: Nam nouus aliquis Mediator dari non potest, vt neque nouum fœdus gratiæ. Sequitur ergo nullum pro peccato hoc reliquum esse sacrificium. Heb. 6. 6.pro eo quod hic dicitur, non adhuc pro peccatis &c. habet fieri non posse vt denuò renouentur per refipiscentiam.
units.tr: If not ) willingly) An argument from the penalty of apostasy and defection, as if he said: if we do not persevere in faith, in hope, in charity, etc., but after receiving the knowledge of the truth sin willingly, then there is no longer, etc. Sin willingly) In these words there is a certain description of apostasy, or defection, or sin against the Holy Spirit. First, it is a sin; then it is a sin against the truth itself, that is, against the Gospel of Christ, for he who sins against the Holy Spirit assails the Gospel itself. Third, it is a sin against the truth of the Gospel once acknowledged, for he who sins against the Holy Spirit sins not out of ignorance but out of knowledge, and against his own conscience. Fourth, the sin is one that is admitted willingly and of one's own accord, that is, from a malicious purpose of mind. For he who sins against the Holy Spirit does not sin from weakness, but from malice and obstinacy of mind. After receiving) that is, after he has once been enlightened and has tasted the heavenly gift. Heb. 6. 4 and following. No longer) that is, there is no sacrifice left by which his sin may be expiated. For if there were one, it would be either the sacrifice of Christ or that of some other new Mediator. But it is not the sacrifice of Christ, for once this sin has been committed, which is called sin against the Holy Spirit, by which the Son of God is trampled underfoot, the blood of the covenant is profaned, and the Spirit of grace is insulted, the sacrifice of Christ no longer pertains to the one who has so sinned, and he who has so sinned loses entirely every right to the sacrifice of Christ. Therefore it is not the sacrifice of Christ by which such a sin is expiated. Nor is it the sacrifice of any other new Mediator by which this sin is expiated, for no new Mediator can be given, any more than a new covenant of grace. It follows, then, that no sacrifice remains for this sin. Heb. 6. 6. In place of what is said here, "no longer a sacrifice for sins", it has "it is impossible that they should be renewed again to repentance".

units.la: 27 Sed horrenda) Hoc alterà pars poenæ est. Nam prima fuit, quòd nulla fit peccati remissio: hæc secunda est, expectatio Iudicij futuri. Hanc horrendam vocat, quia vel ipsa expectatio inferorum horrorem incutit. Porro horrenda expectatio hoc loco nihil aliud videtur esse, quàm metus qui spei opponitur. Nam vt spes est futuri boni, ita metus est futuri mali. Et ignis) Hæc species poenæ est futuræ siue judicij, nempe absumptio per ignis feruorem. Qui devoraturus) Descriptio quædam est feruoris ignis quem dixit, ab effectu suo, qui est in devorandis aduersarijs, hoc est, ijs qui Deo tanquam hosti bellum indicunt, & elata manu peccant.
units.tr: 27 But dreadful) This is the second part of the punishment. For the first was that there is no remission of sin; this second is the expectation of future judgment. He calls it dreadful because even the mere expectation of hell strikes horror. Moreover, a dreadful expectation here seems to be nothing other than the fear which is opposed to hope, for as hope is of a future good, so fear is of a future evil. And fire) This is a kind of future punishment, namely, of judgment, that is, consumption by the fervour of fire. About to devour) This is a description of the fervour of fire which he mentioned, taken from its effect, which is to devour the adversaries, that is, those who declare war on God as an enemy and sin with a raised hand. [About to devour])

units.la: 28 Qui contempserit) Poenam hanc quam dixit confirmat ex minori exemplo ejus, qui contempsit Moßis Legem. Simile argumentum vide Heb. 2. 2. 3. Absque misericordia) Nota quum Deus jubet morte afficere peccatorem, tum praepositeram esse misericordiam qua ei parcitur.
units.tr: 28 He who has set aside) He confirms this punishment which he mentioned from a lesser example, that of him who set aside the Law of Moses. For a similar argument see Heb. 2. 2. 3. Without mercy) Note that when God commands a sinner to be put to death, then mercy by which he is spared is out of place.

units.la: 29 Qui Filium Dei) His omnibus modis peccat apostata, & qui a veritate deficit. Heb. 6. 6. in eundem sensum dicuntur apostatae rursum crucifigere sibimetipsis Filium Dei, & ad ignominiam exponere. Tribus modis dicitur hic peccare apostata. Primum peccat in Christum, qua λόγος est, & Filius Dei. Deinde peccat in Christum, qua homo est crucifixus. Tertio peccat in Spiritum sanctum. Unde apostasia ista vocatur peccatum in Spiritum sanctum.
units.tr: 29 The Son of God) In all these ways the apostate sins, and he who falls away from the truth. Heb. 6. 6. To the same effect, apostates are said to crucify the Son of God again for themselves and to expose him to disgrace. The apostate is said here to sin in three ways. First, he sins against Christ as he is the Word and the Son of God. Second, he sins against Christ as he is the man who was crucified. Third, he sins against the Holy Spirit. Hence this apostasy is called sin against the Holy Spirit.

units.la: 30 Nouimus enim eum) Alterum poenae sive supplicij apostasiae argumentum, à testimonio ipsius Dei, qui profitetur se vltorem omnium peccatorum. Vide Deut. 32. 35. Rom. 12. 19.
units.tr: 30 For we know him who) The second argument for the punishment or penalty of apostasy, drawn from the testimony of God himself, who declares that he is the avenger of all sins. See Deut. 32. 35. Rom. 12. 19.

units.la: 31 Et rursum) Hoc alterum est testimonium idipsum confirmans ex eodem loco. Deut. 32. 36.
units.tr: 31 And again) This second testimony confirms the same point from the same place. Deut. 32. 36.

units.la: Horrendum est) Conclusio est huius loci ἐπιφωνημα τικὸν Dei Vivi) Hoc epitheto viui, ostendit quod dixit, horrendum esse incidere in ejus manus. Nam cum qui manibus quasi suis peccatorem discerpit,adeo viuus fit,&potens ac robustus,necefle est horrendum esse in ejus manus incidere. Sic 2. Theff. 1.9.grauitatem & æternitatem supplicij impiorum arguit à potentia gloriæ Domini.
units.tr: It is a dreadful thing) This is the conclusion of this passage: an exclamation [ἐπιφώνημα] concerning the living God) By this epithet "living" he shows what he said, that it is dreadful to fall into his hands. For since he tears the sinner as if with his own hands, he is so living, so powerful and so strong, that it must indeed be dreadful to fall into his hands. Thus in 2 Thess. 1. 9 he proves the gravity and eternity of the punishment of the wicked from the power of the glory of the Lord.

units.la: 32 Renouocate Vero in memoriam superiores dies, quibus postquam illustrati fuistis, ingens certamen afflictionum sustinuistis.
units.tr: 32 But call to mind the former days, in which, after you were enlightened, you endured a great conflict of afflictions.

units.la: 33 Partim quidem, dum & cum probris, & cum oppressionibus, in theatrum eius produ&li:partim vero, dum socij faëti eius eorum qui in eo statu verfantur.
units.tr: 33 Partly indeed, while you were both made a spectacle of reproaches and oppressions, and partly while you became partners with those who were in that condition.

units.la: 34. Nam & de vinculis meis mecum doluistis, & direptionem facultatum vestrarum cum gaudio accepistis, vt quifciretis vos habere apud vos potiorem substantiam in cælis, & qua permaneat.
units.tr: 34 For you both suffered with me in my bonds, and accepted the plundering of your goods with joy, knowing that you have for yourselves a better substance in heaven, and one that remains.

units.la: 35 Ne igitur abjicite libertatem illam professionem vestram, quæ magnam habet præmij retributionem.
units.tr: 35 Therefore do not cast away that confidence of yours, which has a great reward of recompense.

units.la: 36 Nam patientia vobis est opus, vt voluntatem Dei obfequuti reportetis promissionem.
units.tr: 36 For you have need of patience, so that, having done the will of God, you may obtain the promise.

units.la: 37 Adhuc enim tantillum, tantillum, inquam, & qui venturus est, veniet, neque tardabit.
units.tr: 37 For yet a very little while, a very little while, I say, and he who is coming will come and will not delay.

units.la: 38 Iustus autem ex fide viuet: at fi quis fe subduxerit, non probat eum animus meus.
units.tr: 38 But the just shall live by faith; but if anyone draws back, my soul has no pleasure in him.

units.la: 39 At nos non fumus qui nos subducamus ad exitium, sed qui credamus ad animæ salutem.
units.tr: 39 But we are not of those who draw back to destruction, but of those who believe to the saving of the soul.

units.la: Renouocate Vero) Dehortatur à defectione fiue apostasia, & hortatur ad perseuerantiam, ab af- flictioni-
units.tr: But call to mind) He dissuades them from defection or apostasy and exhorts them to perseverance, by recalling the afflictions

units.la: flictionibus quas superioribus diebus pro fide sunt perpessi. Nam non decet eos tam multa passos esse frustra. Gal.3.4. Propositio exhortationis hoc loco est, ut reuocent in memoriam superiores dies: non enim e memoria nostra excidere debet superior nostra conditio, siue prospera siue aduersa. Mementote vos quondam Gentes in carne. Eph.2.11.12. Quibus post quam) Definitio quaedam est superiorum dierum, ab afflictionibus quibus illis diebus exercitati sunt. Illustrati fuistis) Tempus afflictionum notat, quod erat non ante fidem, sed post fidem & illuminationem. Nam fidem & illuminationem mentis sequitur Crux, Dei consilio immissa ad fidem explorandam. Certamen vocat afflictionum, quia cum afflictionibus certamus & conflictamur in hac vita.
units.tr: which they endured for the faith in former days. For it is not fitting that they, having suffered so much, should have suffered in vain. Gal. 3.4. The proposition of this exhortation is that they should recall the former days, for our former condition, whether prosperous or adverse, ought not to slip from our memory. Remember that you were once Gentiles in the flesh. Eph. 2.11, 12. After they had been enlightened) This is a certain definition of the former days, by the afflictions with which they were exercised in those days. You were enlightened) Indicates the time of the afflictions, which was not before faith but after faith and illumination. For the cross follows faith and the illumination of the mind, sent by God's counsel to test the faith. He calls the afflictions a contest, because in this life we contend with afflictions and struggle against them.

units.la: 33 Partim quidem) Distributione explicat afflictiones quas dixit: partim erant afflictiones quas ipsi perpessi sunt, partim erant θεατρίζοντες, qua cum afflictis aliis doluerunt. Cum probris) Afflictionem quam ipsi perpessi sunt in eo ponit, quod producti sint in theatrum cum probris & oppressionibus, h. e. quod publice & inspectante quasi mundo, & probrose, & injuriose tractati sunt. Ergo productio haec in publicum, & quasi in theatrum, auget & exaggerat duo illa afflictionum genera, nempe probrum & oppressiones. Dum loci) In hanc sententiam loqui videtur Paulus 2. Timoth. 1. 8. cùm monet Timotheum ne pudeat eum ipsius,qui tum erat captiuus Christi, sed potius sit particeps afflictionum Euangelij.
units.tr: 33 Partly indeed) By distribution he explains the afflictions he had mentioned: partly they were afflictions which they themselves suffered, and partly they were those made a spectacle [θεατρίζοντες], in which they grieved with others who were afflicted. With reproaches) He places the affliction they themselves suffered in this, that they were brought out into the theatre with reproaches and oppressions, that is, that they were treated publicly, as if before the watching world, shamefully and injuriously. Therefore this bringing forth into public, as if into a theatre, increases and magnifies those two kinds of affliction, namely reproach and oppressions. Likewise in place) Paul seems to speak to this effect in 2 Tim. 1.8, when he admonishes Timothy not to be ashamed of him, who was then a prisoner of Christ, but rather to be a partaker of the afflictions of the gospel.

units.la: 34. Nam (tr-de Vinculis) Κατὰ ὑςτερῶσιν explicat superiora afflictionum membra : posteriusenim priori loco declarat, prius autem posterior.De Vinculis) De συμπαθεία hac vide Rom. 12.15.Flete cum flentibus. Cum gaudio) Non dicit simpliciter perpessos, esse eos direptionem facultatum suarum; verùm addit, cum gaudio perpessos. Hoc eorum afflictionem commendat. In martyrio duo requiruntur: Primùm, vt sit bona caussa : Secundum, vt adsit gaudium. Vtrumque complexus est Petrus 1. Epist. 4.16. Sed si (inquit) vt Christianus affligitur aliquis, ne pudefiat, imò glorificet Deum tanquam Patrem. Quibus verbis habes & martyrij caussam optimam, nempe fidem Christi, & gaudium quo afficidebet animus in martyrio. Vt quisciretis) Ratio cur cum gaudio acceperint direptionem facultatum suarum, à fide & spe quam habebant, adepturos se cœlestem substantiam, quam cum terrenis facultatibus comparat Apostolus, & in bonitate, & in stabilitate. Quod ad bonitatem potior est : quod ad stabilitatem permanet in æternum.
units.tr: 34. For (on those in bonds) By hysteron proteron [Κατὰ ὑςτερῶσιν] he explains the preceding members of the afflictions: for the latter clause declares the former, and the former the latter. On those in bonds) On this sympathy see Rom. 12.15, Weep with those who weep. With joy) He does not simply say they were despoiled of their goods; he adds that they endured it with joy. This commends their affliction. Two things are required in martyrdom: first, that the cause be good; second, that joy be present. Peter comprehends both, 1 Pet. 4.16: But if anyone suffers as a Christian, let him not be ashamed, but let him glorify God as Father. In these words you have both the best cause of martyrdom, namely faith in Christ, and the joy with which the mind ought to be affected in martyrdom. That you might know) The reason they accepted the plundering of their goods with joy is the faith and hope they had, that they would obtain a heavenly substance, which the Apostle compares with earthly goods, both in goodness and in stability. As to goodness, the heavenly is the better; as to stability, it remains for ever.

units.la: 35 Ne igitur) Concludit principalem exhortationem : perstandum nimirum esse in fide siue fiducia. Qua) Argumentum exhortationis duodecimum, à mercede fidei. Nota mercedę esse, non operum nostrorum, sed fidei, h. e. meriti Christi, quod fide apprehenditur.
units.tr: 35 Therefore) He concludes the principal exhortation: namely, that one must persevere in faith or confidence. Which) The twelfth argument of the exhortation, from the reward of faith. Note that the reward is not of our works but of faith, that is, of the merit of Christ, which is apprehended by faith.

units.la: Nam patientia) Occupatio. Obiici enim poterat: Dicis fiduciam habere magnam præmij retributionem: nos vero fiduciæ siue fidei nullū fructū percipimus præter afflictiones. Respondet. Credentibus opus esse patientia. Vt vbi) Quo fine sit opus patientia ostendit. Nempe vt posteaquam ex voluntate Dei perpessi fuerint afflictiones, reportet promissionem, h.e. promissam mercedem. Nota, promissiones vitæ æternæ fiunt cū exceptione afflictionum. Quamobrem cū fide in promissiones, necessario coniungenda est patientia, cuius beneficio duramus sub afflictionibus.
units.tr: For patience) Anticipation. For it could be objected: you say that confidence has a great recompense; but we perceive no fruit from confidence or faith except afflictions. He replies that believers have need of patience. So that) He shows for what end patience is needed: namely, that after they have suffered afflictions by the will of God, they may receive back the promise, that is, the promised reward. Note that the promises of eternal life are made with the exception of afflictions. Therefore patience must necessarily be joined with faith in the promises, by whose benefit we endure under afflictions.

units.la: Adhuc enim) Altera occupatio. At tardat Dominus; ac proinde, non nisi tarde reportaturi sumus promissam mercedem? Respondet, paululum admodum temporis adhuc superesse dum veniat Dominus. vide 2. Pet. 3. 9.
units.tr: For yet) Another anticipation. But the Lord delays; and so shall we receive the promised reward only late? He replies that there is still a very little time left until the Lord comes. See 2 Pet. 3.9.

units.la: Iustus autem) Cui demùm tribuenda sit vita in aduentu Domini ostendit, nempe ei qui iustus est, hoc est, fide Christi iustificatus, is ex fide illa qua iustificatus est viuet.
units.tr: But the just) He shows to whom life is finally to be given at the coming of the Lord: to him who is just, that is, justified by the faith of Christ, who shall live by that faith by which he is justified.

units.la: At si quis) E diuerso docet cui non sit tribuenda vita in aduentu Domini, ei nimirum vita non est adiudicanda qui se subduxerit, h. e. qui à fide defecerit. Non probat) Pro eo quod dicendum erat non viuet, dixit, non probare
units.tr: But if anyone) On the contrary he teaches to whom life is not to be given at the coming of the Lord: namely, life is not to be adjudged to him who has drawn back, that is, who has fallen away from faith. Does not please) Instead of what ought to have been said, "shall not live," he said "his soul does not take pleasure in him,"

units.la: L eum animam ipsius. Hic versus desumptus est ex Propheta Abacuc. cap. 2. verf 4. vbi legitur. Ecce ebullat in quo no est rectus animus ipsius: iustus autem ex fide sua viuet. Verum Apostolus hoc loco verba Prophetae non adduxit ex profesto, sed talem sententiam accommodauit hominibus sui temporis, qualem Propheta olim accommodauit ijs qui prisco illo seculo vixerunt. Atque hic habes argumentum principalis exhortationis decimumtertium.
units.tr: that is, his soul. This verse is taken from the prophet Habakkuk, chap. 2, verse 4, where it reads: Behold, he whose soul is puffed up is not upright in himself; but the righteous shall live by his faith. But the Apostle did not bring forward the words of the Prophet expressly, but applied such a sentiment to the men of his own time as the Prophet once applied to those who lived in that ancient age. And here you have the argument of the principal exhortation, the thirteenth.

units.la: 39. Atnos non) Correctio est & mitigatio superioris sententiae, quae fortassis durior ac seuerior videri potuit. Hac igitur correctione Hebraeos eximit e numero Apostatarum, & credentibus accenset. Ad exitium) Obscure deterret ab apostasia & defectione a fide, arguméto ab exitio illo quod manet Apostatas. Ad animae salutem) Obscure ad perseuerantiam in fide Hebraeos excitat, argumento a salute illa aeterna, quae manet credentes.
units.tr: 39. But we are not) This is a correction and softening of the preceding sentence, which perhaps seemed rather harsh and severe. By this correction he removes the Hebrews from the number of apostates and counts them among believers. To destruction) He obliquely deters them from apostasy and falling away from faith, by the argument of that destruction which awaits apostates. To the salvation of the soul) He obliquely stirs the Hebrews to perseverance in faith, by the argument of that eternal salvation which awaits believers.

units.la: Argumentum Capitis Vndecimi.
units.tr: The Argument of Chapter Eleven.

units.la: Hoc capite digressio est in commendationem fidei, ad quam hactenus est hortatus. Eam autem commendat ab effectis, primum generalibus ad versum 4. deinde specialibus, a versu 4. ad finem capitis.
units.tr: This chapter is a digression in commendation of faith, to which he has so far been exhorting. He commends it from its effects: first general ones, up to verse 4, then particular ones, from verse 4 to the end of the chapter.

units.la: CAPVT XI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XI.

units.la: 1 Est autem fides, illud quod extant quae sperantur, & quae demonstrat quae non videntur.
units.tr: 1 Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.

units.la: 2 Ob eam enim testimonio sunt ornati maiores.
units.tr: 2 For by it our forefathers were commended.

units.la: 3 Per fidem intelligimus constructum fuisse mundum verbo Dei, ut quae cernimus non sint ex apparentibus facta.
units.tr: 3 Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that the things which are seen were not made of things which do appear.

units.la: Est autem fides Digreditur in commendationem fidei illius, ad quam hactenus est hortatus: commendatio est ab effectis, primum generalibus, tribus primis versibus. Primum effectum generale est quod fides fit substantia eorum quae sperantur, hoc est, existere faciat res quae nondum sunt, sed quae sperantur. Fides existere facit ea quae nondum sunt, ex parte, non autem secundum se tota: nam dum credimus in promissiones de vita futura, praesens quaedam est illius vitae fruitio. Et quod demonstrat (Idem re aliis verbis repetitur: ἐλέγχος) hoc demonstrationem vocat, quia ex parte oculis animi repraesentat ea, quae secundum se tota non videntur: nam ut dum credimus in promissiones de vita aeterna, tunc eius ex parte est fruitio & participatio: ita eiusdem aspectus est ex parte. Quae non videntur hoc loco, sunt eadem quae sperantur: nam quod non videmus speramus. Rom. 8. 25. Hoc igitur loco innuit Apostolus admirabilem esse fidei efficaciam, qua fit ut quae non subsistunt subsistant, quae non videntur videantur. Quibus verbis nihil aliud significat, quam per fidem inchoari in hac vita vitam illam aeternam.
units.tr: Now faith is He digresses into a commendation of that faith to which he has been exhorting until now. He commends it by its effects, first the general ones, in the first three verses. The first general effect is that faith is the substance of things hoped for, that is, it makes things which do not yet exist, but are hoped for, to exist. Faith makes those things exist in part, but not wholly in themselves, for while we believe the promises about future life, there is a present enjoyment of that life. And the evidence (the same thing is repeated in other words: [ἔλεγχος]). He calls it evidence because in part it sets before the eyes of the mind things which are not wholly seen in themselves. For just as, while we believe the promises of eternal life, we have in part the enjoyment and participation of it, so in part there is a sight of it. The things not seen in this place are the same as the things hoped for, for what we do not see we hope for (Rom. 8. 25). Here, then, the Apostle implies that the efficacy of faith is wonderful, so that things which do not subsist come to subsist, and things which are not seen come to be seen. By these words he means nothing other than that eternal life is begun in this life through faith.

units.la: 2 Ob eam) Secundum effectum generale, fides maiorum, siue Patrum effecit vt testimonio honorifico aliquo sint ornati. Hoc videbimus postea in inductione particularium fidei effectorum. Nota: Commendatio piorum in veteri & noua Scriptura est ex fide proprie. Si quae sit ex operibus expressa commendatio, ea est qua per opera tanquam effecta notiora, arguitur & ostenditur fides. Ergo commendatio est ex operibus, non tanquam causis, sed effectis & testimonijs fidei in Christum, quae vera est commendationis omnis causa.
units.tr: 2 For by it) The second general effect: the faith of the forefathers, or Fathers, has brought it about that they were adorned with some honourable testimony. We shall see this later, in the enumeration of the particular effects of faith. Note: the commendation of the godly in the Old and New Scripture is properly from faith. If there is any explicit commendation from works, it is that by which faith is argued for and shown through works, as more known effects. Therefore the commendation is from works, not as causes, but as effects and testimonies of faith in Christ, which is the true cause of all commendation.

units.la: 3 Per fidem) Tertium effectum fidei generale. Beneficio fidei non tantum videmus apprehendimúsque futura, vt in primo effectu, sed videmus etiam quae multis retro seculis facta sunt. Videmus ipsam mundi creationem, imò per fidem videmus quae ante tempora seculària in aeterno Dei consilio fuerunt; vt electionem & praedestinationem nostram. Verbo Dei) Per fidem non tantum intelligimus mundum constructum fuisse, verum constructu fuisse solo verbo & nutu Dei, neque id modo, sed ex nihilo fuisse constructum. Vt qua) Sensus est, ac si diceret: adeo vt mundus ille quem cernimus, non sit ex aliqua apparente ac subsistente materia, sed ex nihilo, conditus. Videntur haec verba ῥήματικὰ subiecta esse superioribus. Habet enim quandam exclamationis & admirationis speciem.
units.tr: 3 Through faith) The third general effect of faith. By the benefit of faith we not only see and grasp future things, as in the first effect, but we also see things that were done many ages ago. We see the very creation of the world, and indeed through faith we see those things which were before the ages of time in the eternal counsel of God, such as our election and predestination. Through the word of God) Through faith we understand not only that the world was framed, but that it was framed by the word and nod of God alone, and not only so, but that it was made out of nothing. So that) The sense is as if he were saying: so that that world which we see is not made out of any visible and subsisting matter, but was fashioned out of nothing. These words seem to be attached to what precedes them as an exclamation. They have a certain appearance of exclamation and wonder.

units.la: 4 Abel per fidem, maiorem pretij sacrificium obtuobtulit Deo quàm Cain: per quam testimonium obtinuit quod esset iustus, testimonium perhibente Deo de donis eius : & per hanc mortuus adhuc loquitur.
units.tr: 4 By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts; and by it he being dead yet speaketh.

units.la: 5 Per fidem Enoch fuit translatus, ne videret mortem: nec fuit inuentus, propterea quod transtulerat eum Deus : priusquam enim transferretur, testimonii obtinuerat quod placuisset Deo.
units.tr: 5 By faith Enoch was translated, that he should not see death; and was not found, because God had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God.

units.la: 6 Atqui fieri non potest ut sine fide quisquam ei placeat : nam qui accedit ad Deum, hunc crede- re oportet esse Deum, & præmia largiri ijs qui ipsum requirunt.
units.tr: 6 But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.

units.la: 7 Per fidem diuinitus admonitus Noe de iis quæ nondum videbantur, veritus, apparauit arcam ad seruandam domum suam : per quam arcam condénauit mundum, & eius quæ ex fide est iustitiæ sàstus est hæres.
units.tr: 7 By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by which ark he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith.

units.la: 8 Per fide vocatus Abraham auscultauit Deo ut abiret in locum quem acceptURUS erat in hæreditate: & exiuit, nescieṅs quo esset venturus.
units.tr: 8 By faith Abraham, when he was called, obeyed God and went out to a place which he should after receive for an inheritance; and he went out, not knowing whither he went.

units.la: 9 Per fidem commoratus est in terra promissa ut aliena, commoratus est in Tabernaculis cum Isaac & Iacob coheredibus eiusdem promissionis
units.tr: 9 By faith he sojourned in the land of promise as in a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise.

units.la: 10 Expectabat enim urbem habentem fundamenta, cuius artifex & conditor est Deus.
units.tr: 10 For he looked for a city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God.

units.la: 11 Per fidem & ipsa Sara vim ad concipiendum semen accepit, ac præter ætatis rationem peperit : quòd fidelem esse duxerit eum qui promiserat.
units.tr: 11 Through faith also Sara herself received strength to conceive seed, and was delivered of a child when she was past age, because she judged him faithful who had promised.

units.la: 12 Quapropter & ex Vno, eoque iam emortua, nati sunt posteri, quanta est astrorum caeli multitudo, & quasi arena illa innumerabilis qua est ad oram maris.
units.tr: 12 Therefore sprang there even of one, and him as good as dead, so many as the stars of the sky in multitude, and as the sand which is by the sea shore innumerable.

units.la: 13 Secundum fidem mortui sunt isti omnes non adepti promissa, sed eminus ea conspicati, postquam ipsi fuissent persuasi, & ea amplexi essent ac profesi fuissent se hospites & advenas esse in terra.
units.tr: 13 These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off, were assured of them, and embraced them, and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.

units.la: 14 Nam qui haec dicunt, palam ostendunt se patriam quaerere.
units.tr: 14 For they that say such things declare plainly that they seek a country.

units.la: 15 Quod si illius memores fuissent ex quae exierant, habere poterant tempus ad revertendum.
units.tr: 15 And truly, if they had been mindful of that country from which they came out, they might have had opportunity to have returned.

units.la: 16 Atqui meliorem expetunt, hoc est, caelestem, quapropter non dedignatur ipse Deus, cognominari Deus eorum: parauerat enim eis urbem.
units.tr: 16 But now they desire a better country, that is, an heavenly: wherefore God is not ashamed to be called their God: for he hath prepared for them a city.

units.la: 17 Abraham quum tentaretur, obtulit Isaac per fidem, unigenitum, inquam, illum obtulit, qui promissiones exceperat.
units.tr: 17 By faith Abraham, when he was tried, offered up Isaac; and he that had received the promises offered up his only begotten son.

units.la: 18 Ad quem dictum fuerat, in Isaac vocabitur tibi semen.
units.tr: 18 Of whom it was said, That in Isaac shall thy seed be called.

units.la: 19 Cum ratiocinatus statuisset, Deum vel a mortuis excitare posse: unde etiam illum similitudine quadam recepit.
units.tr: 19 Accounting that God was able to raise him up, even from the dead; from whence also he received him in a figure.

units.la: 20 Per fidem de futuris benedixit Isaac filio Iacobo & Esau.
units.tr: 20 By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things to come.

units.la: 21 Per fidem, Iacob moriens singulis filiis Ioseph benedixit, & adorauit baculo innixus.
units.tr: 21 By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed both the sons of Joseph, and worshipped, leaning upon the top of his staff.

units.la: 22 Per fidem, Ioseph moriens de egressione filiorum Israel meminit, deque ossibus suis mandauit.
units.tr: 22 By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Israel, and gave commandment concerning his bones.

units.la: 23 Per fidem, Moses quum natus effet, occul-tatus est menses tres a parentibus suis, quod viderent enuftum esse puerulum, & non timuerunt edictum regis.
units.tr: 23 By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months of his parents, because they saw that he was a proper child; and they were not afraid of the king's commandment.

units.la: 24 Per fidem, Moses iam grandis renuit vocari filius filia Pharaonis.
units.tr: 24 By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter;

units.la: 25 Potius eligens simul malis vexari cum populo Dei, quam temporariam retinere peccati fruitionem,
units.tr: 25 Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season;

units.la: 26 Maiores arbitratus diuitias probrū Christi, quam thesauros Aegyptiorum. Intuebatur enim in premij largitionem.
units.tr: 26 Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward.

units.la: 27 Per fidem reliquit Aegyptum, nihil timens iram regis: nam vt qui videret eum qui est inuisibilis, ita forti animo fuit.
units.tr: 27 By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible.

units.la: 28 Per fidem peregit pascha & effusionem sanguinis, ne qui perimebat primogenita, ipsos angeret.
units.tr: 28 Through faith he kept the passover, and the sprinkling of blood, lest he that destroyed the firstborn should touch them.

units.la: 29 Per fidem transierunt rubrum mare velut per siccam terram: cuius maris faelo periculo Aegypti absorpti sunt.
units.tr: 29 By faith they passed through the Red sea as by dry land, which the Egyptians assaying to do were drowned.

units.la: 30 Per fidem moenia Iericho conciderunt, quae circundata fuissent ad dies septem.
units.tr: 30 By faith the walls of Jericho fell down, after they were compassed about seven days.

units.la: 31 Per fidem, Rahab meretrix illa non periit cum iis qui non obedierant, quia pacifice exceptit hospitio exploratores.
units.tr: 31 By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace.

units.la: 32 Et quid praeterea loquor? deficiet enim me commemorantem de Gedeone, de Barac, Sampsone, Iephthe, Dauide, & Samuele, ac Prophetis.
units.tr: 32 And what shall I say more? For the time would fail me to tell of Gideon, and of Barak, and of Samson, and of Jephthah, of David also, and Samuel, and of the prophets.

units.la: 33 Qui per fidem debellarunt regna, exercuerunt iustitiam, assecuti sunt promissiones, occluserunt ora leonum.
units.tr: 33 Who through faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions,

units.la: 34 Extinxerunt vim ignis, effugerunt acies gladij, validi facti sunt ex imbecillis, effecti sunt robusti in bello, exercitus exterorum in fugam verterunt.
units.tr: 34 Quenched the violence of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, out of weakness were made strong, waxed valiant in fight, turned to flight the armies of the aliens.

units.la: 35 Mulieres acceperunt ex resurrectione mortuos suos: alij vero distenti sunt neglecta liberatione, ut potiorem resurrectionem nanciscerentur.
units.tr: 35 Women received their dead raised to life again; and others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection.

units.la: 36 Alij rursus ludibria, et flagella sunt experti, insuper et vincula et carcerem.
units.tr: 36 Others again experienced mockings and scourgings, and moreover chains and prison.

units.la: 37 Lapidati sunt, dissecti sunt, tentati sunt, gladio caesi occubuerunt, oberrauerunt cum ovillis et caprinis pellibus, destituti, oppressi, male vexati.
units.tr: 37 They were stoned, they were sawn asunder, they were tempted, they were slain by the sword; they wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins, destitute, oppressed, badly treated.

units.la: 38 Quibus indignus erat mundus: in desertis errantes, et montibus ac speluncis, et cavernis terrae.
units.tr: 38 Of whom the world was not worthy: wandering in deserts, and on mountains and in caves and holes of the earth.

units.la: 39 Atque omnes hi testimonium adepti per fidem, non obtinuerunt promissum illud.
units.tr: 39 And all these, though they obtained a testimony through faith, did not obtain that promise.

units.la: 40 Quod Deus de nobis melius quoddam providerat, ne absque nobis consecrarentur.
units.tr: 40 Because God had provided something better concerning us, so that apart from us they should not be made perfect.

units.la: Abel per fidem ) Sequuntur particularia fidei effecta, ex quibus eam commendat. Particularia voco effecta, ea quae sunt fidei certarum quarundam personarum. Ac primum quidem habemus effecta fidei particularia quorundam Patrum, qui vixerunt primo illo mundi seculo ante diluuiũ,nimirũ Abelis,Enochi,& Noahi. Fide Abelis tria hîc numerantur effectu:primũ est , quod fides ejus effecerit vt maioris precij sacrificiũ obtulerit Deo,quàm Cain.Per fidem enim,primùm placuit Deo persona,deinde oblatio. Per quam) Secundum est effectum fidei Abelis,obtinuit testimonium quod justus effet. Hoc pertinet ad illustrandum fecundum illud effectũ generale,de quo suprà v.2. Testimonii) Ostendit proximũ effectũ fiue teftimoniũ juftitiæ, quod obtinuit Abel,ex testimonio quod Deus perhibuit de donis ejus, h.e.de sacrificio ab eo oblato. Nihil expressé legitur in Genes. de hoc testimonio,verùm probabile est ex collatione similium exemplorũ:vt Aaronis Leuit. 9. 24. Eliæ 1. Reg. 18.38.Dauidis 1.Paralip.21. 28.Solomonis 2. Para.7.1.probabile (inquam) est,sacrificium illius igne cœlitus demisso,consumptum fuisse. Et per) Tertium est effectum fidei Abelis:fides ejus facit vt, licèt jampridem fit mortuus, tamen adhuc viuat quodammodò & loquatur. Vide infrà 12.24.vide Genef.4.10. vbi dicitur sanguinem Abelis vindicta à Deo poscere.
units.tr: Abel by faith) They now follow the particular effects of faith, by which the author commends it. I call them particular effects those which belong to the faith of certain individuals. And first we have the particular effects of faith of certain Fathers who lived in that first age of the world before the flood, namely Abel, Enoch and Noah. Three effects of Abel's faith are listed here. The first is that his faith caused him to offer to God a sacrifice of greater worth than Cain's. For by faith God was first pleased with the person, and then with the offering. By which) The second effect of Abel's faith: he obtained the testimony that he was righteous. This belongs to illustrating that second general effect, of which above at verse 2. Of testimony) He shows the nearer effect, or testimony of righteousness, which Abel obtained from the testimony God gave concerning his gifts, that is, concerning the sacrifice offered by him. Nothing is expressly read in Genesis about this testimony, but it is probable from comparison with similar examples: as with Aaron, Lev. 9.24; Elijah, 1 Kings 18.38; David, 1 Chron. 21.28; Solomon, 2 Chron. 7.1. It is probable, I say, that his sacrifice, with fire sent down from heaven, was consumed. And by) The third effect of Abel's faith: his faith makes it so that, although he died long ago, yet he still lives and speaks, as it were. See below, 12.24; see Gen. 4.10, where it is said that the blood of Abel calls for vengeance from God.

units.la: 5 Per fidem Enoch) Sequitur particulare efsectum fidei Enochi, sursum assumptus est à Deo. Ne videret) Finis,vt eriperetur à morte. Nec fuit ) Illustratio translationis siue assumptiónis ejus,ex eo quod eam sequutum est. Sic translatus est vt amplius non fuerit inuentus. Propterea)Ratio cur non fuerit inuentus: quem enim Deus transtulit & assumpsit, quis inuenire potest? Priusquam) Probat per fidem suisse translatum, hoc syllogismo. Fieri non potest vt quisquam sine fide Deo placeat: atqui Enoch priusquam transferretur testimonium obtinuerat quòd Deo placuisset: Ergo per fidem placuit Deo, & ex consequenti per fidem translatus fuit. Assumptio praecedit, Propositio sequitur initio sequentis versus. De translatione Enochi habes Genef.5.22.& deinceps, vbi scribit Moses eum continenter ambulasse cum Deo: pro quo dicit hic Apostolus eum placuisse Deo. Testimonium obtinuerat) Hoc pertinet ad illustrandum generale fidei essectum secundum.
units.tr: 5 By faith Enoch) Follows the particular effect of Enoch's faith: he was taken up by God. That he should not see) The purpose: that he might be taken away from death. And was not) An illustration of his translation or assumption, from the fact that it followed it. Thus he was translated, so that he was no more found. Therefore) The reason why he was not found: for who can find him whom God has translated and taken up? Before) He proves that he was translated by faith, by this syllogism. It cannot be that anyone should please God without faith; but Enoch, before he was translated, had obtained the testimony that he pleased God; therefore by faith he pleased God, and consequently by faith he was translated. The minor premise comes first, and the major premise follows at the beginning of the next verse. On Enoch's translation you have Gen. 5.22 and following, where Moses writes that he walked continually with God; for which this Apostle says that he pleased God. Had obtained the testimony) This belongs to illustrating the second general effect of faith.

units.la: 6 Nam qui accedit)Ratio propositionis, quasi dicat, cui in animo est placere Deo, oportet eum credere, &c. Accedere enim ad Deum hoc loco est ei placere. Duo sunt hic de Deo credenda. Primum est quòd sit Deus: Secundum est quòd talis sit, h. e. justus sit ac benignus in eos qui ipsum requirunt. Quod de Deo primùm credendum est, ad eius naturam spectat absolute in se consideratam: quod verò de Deo secundò credendum est, de Deo est, non absolute in se considerato, sed vt sese ad nos demittit.
units.tr: 6 For he who comes) The reason for the proposition, as if to say: he who has in mind to please God must believe, etc. For to come to God here means to please him. Two things are to be believed about God here. The first is that God exists; the second is that he is such, that is, that he is righteous and kind toward those who seek him. What is to be believed about God first concerns his nature considered absolutely in himself; but what is to be believed about God secondly is about God not considered absolutely in himself, but as he lowers himself to us.

units.la: 7 Per fidem) Hoc tertium est particulare efsectum fidei, nempe Noæ. Objectu fidei Noæ fuit uit diuina admonitio, quam dicit fuisse de ijs ebus, quæ nondum cernebantur, nempe de illuuio post annos centum viginti eventuro. Vide Genef. 6. Porrò hæc verba indicant effectum hoc speciale fidei Noę pertinere ad illuftrandum generale illud effectum fidei primum. Veritus) Hoc primum est fidei Noæ effectum, interna nimirum reuerentia & obedientia Apparauit arcam) Secundum effectum fidei Noæ, externa obedientia in arca apparanda. Ad feruandam) Secundum hoc effectum illustrat, primùm suo fine, ad feruandam familiam suam ab aquarum diluuio, quod Dei verbo credens certò futurum expectabat. Per quam arcam) Deinde illustrat hoc effectum ex duobus alijs effectis ipsum consequentibus. Primum respicit prisum illum mundum, quem condemnauit per arcam illam. Nam Noæ duabus rebus inexcusabilem fecit prisum illum mundum, primùm verbo à se prædicato, (quo hortatus est ad resipiscentiam, vt venturum judicium effugerent, fuit enim præco justitiæ. 2 Pet. 2. 5.) propterea quòd ei non adhibita fides. Deinde verbo, ad ipsius veritatem confirmandam, adjecit sacramentum, arcam: vt tum verbo, tum sacramento, prisum illum mundum condemnaret. Fteiu qua) Alterum effectum arcæ apparationem consequens, ipsum Noe respicit, ipsius nimirum justificatio & salus, prisci mundi condemnationi opposita. Nam factus est hæres ejus quæ per fidem est justitiæ.Iustitiam intelligo imputatam quæ Christus tanquam hæreditatem impertit omnibus,qui per fidem ipsum apprehendunt.
units.tr: 7 By faith) This is the third particular effect of faith, namely Noah's. The object of Noah's faith was the divine warning, concerning things not yet seen, namely the flood that was to come after one hundred and twenty years. See Gen. 6. Moreover, these words indicate that this particular effect of Noah's faith belongs to illustrating that first general effect of faith. Moved with reverence) This is the first effect of Noah's faith: inner reverence and obedience. Prepared the ark) The second effect of Noah's faith: outward obedience in preparing the ark. To save) He illustrates this second effect, first by its purpose: to save his household from the flood of waters, which he, believing God's word, expected to come with certainty. By which ark) Then he illustrates this effect by two other effects that follow from it. The first concerns that former world, which he condemned by that ark. For Noah made the former world inexcusable in two ways: first by the word he preached (by which he exhorted them to repentance, so that they might escape the coming judgment; for he was a herald of righteousness, 2 Pet. 2.5), because it was not received with faith; and then, to confirm the truth of his word, he added a sacrament, the ark, so that by both word and sacrament he might condemn that former world. Of that righteousness which is by faith) The other effect, following from the preparation of the ark, concerns Noah himself: namely his justification and salvation, set over against the condemnation of the former world. For he became heir of that righteousness which is by faith. By righteousness I understand the imputed righteousness which Christ bestows as an inheritance on all who lay hold of him through faith.

units.la: 8 Per fidem vocatus) Hactenus fuerunt essecta fidei particularia Patrum quorundam qui vixerunt ante diluuium. Sequuntur effecta fidei particularia Patrum quorundam qui vixerunt post diluuium, vsque ad exitum populi ex Ægypto : & primum quidem Abrahami, qui Pater credentium vocatur.Rom.4.11.Essectum fidei Abrahami, est obedientia Dei voci præstita, quòd Deo ipsum vocanti ex Vrė Chaldæorum auscultauerit. Vt abiret) Descriptio quædam obedientiæ Abrahami, quæ ostenditur in quo posita fuerit hęc obedientia, in eo nimirùm quod abierit in eum locum, quem accepturus erat in hæreditatem,h.e. terram Canaan,quæ typus erat cœlorum. Et exiit nesciens) Amplificat illam obedientiam Abrahami ab ignoratione loci in quem venturus erat, Deus non nominauit ei locum quo iturus effet,sed dixit ei,Abi in eam terram quam monstraturus sum tibi.Genef.12.1.Abrahamus nihil cunctatus, in hac Dei vocatione acquieuit, & Deum vocante quasi clausis oculis secutus est, paratus ire quocunque ipsum duceret.
units.tr: 8 By faith Abraham was called) Thus far have been the particular effects of faith of certain Fathers who lived before the flood. Now follow the particular effects of faith of certain Fathers who lived after the flood, down to the exodus of the people from Egypt; and first of Abraham, who is called the father of believers, Rom. 4.11. The effect of Abraham's faith is obedience rendered to God's voice, in that he obeyed God calling him out of Ur of the Chaldeans. That he should go out) A certain description of Abraham's obedience, showing in what this obedience consisted, namely in that he went out to the place which he was to receive as an inheritance, that is, the land of Canaan, which was a type of heaven. And went out not knowing) He amplifies that obedience of Abraham by his ignorance of the place to which he was to come. God did not name for him the place to which he was to go, but said to him: Go into the land which I will show you, Gen. 12.1. Abraham, without hesitation, acquiesced in this call of God and followed God calling him as if with his eyes closed, ready to go wherever he should lead him.

units.la: 9 Per fidem commoratus) Secundum effectum fidei Abrahami. Non tantum per fidem abiit in terram promissam,sed etiam per fidem in ea commo ommoratus eft. Vt aliena} Exaggerat hoc effectum commorationis in terra promiffa, ex duplici ipfius modo.Primùm commoratus eft in ea vt aliena.Quamuis enim ad ipfum vi promiffionis Dei jure fpectabat, tamen Abrahamus fe inquilinum & peregrinum in ea profefus eft. Genef. 23. 4. In tabernaculis) Alter commorationis modus: Commoratus eft in tabernaculis, vt hoc quafi facramento obignaret quod profeffus eft, oftenderetque fe ftabilem fibi fedem in ea regione nô fixiffe, fed in ea peregrinari. Cum Ifaac) Illuftrat hunc alterum commorationis Abrahami modum, à fimili exemplo filij & nepotis, Ifaaci & Iacobi; vbi obiter vides fpeciale hoc effectû fidei Abrahami, cum Ifaaco & Iacobo communicari. Coharedibus) Defcriptio eft Ifaaci & Iacobi: quòd hæredes fuerint ejufdem cum Abrahamo promiffionis. Nam facta eft promiffio terræ illius, non foli Abrahamo, fed & femini ipfius, & eadem promiffio Ifaaco & Iacobo aliquoties repetita eft. Gen. 26. 3. & 28. 13. & 35. 12.
units.tr: 9 By faith he sojourned) The second effect of Abraham's faith. He went into the promised land not only by faith, but by faith he also sojourned there. As strangers) He magnifies this effect of sojourning in the promised land by a twofold manner. First, he sojourned in it as strangers: for although by the force of God's promise it belonged to him by right, yet Abraham professed himself a sojourner and stranger in it, Gen. 23.4. In tents) The other manner of sojourning: he dwelt in tents, so that by this, as it were a sacrament, he might seal what he professed, and show that he had not fixed a settled seat for himself in that region, but was a pilgrim there. With Isaac) He illustrates this second manner of Abraham's sojourning by the similar example of son and grandson, Isaac and Jacob; where, incidentally, you see this special effect of Abraham's faith shared with Isaac and Jacob. Fellow heirs) A description of Isaac and Jacob: that they were heirs of the same promise as Abraham. For the promise of that land was made not only to Abraham but also to his seed, and the same promise was repeated several times to Isaac and Jacob, Gen. 26.3; 28.13; 35.12.

units.la: 10 Expectabat enim) Ratio cur Abrahamus in terra promiffa commoratus fit in tabernaculis: à fpe vrbis firmioris. Expectabat vrbem habentem fundamenta, propterea nolebat fixam fibi fedem in terra promiffa ftatuere, fed contentus fuit commorari in tabernaculis. Per vrbem habentem fundamenta intelligit cœlû, quod eodem sensu vocatur regnum quod concuti non potest, Heb. 12. 28. Cujus Sacramentum erat terra illa Canaan. Nota igitur veteres illos Patriarchas non acquieuiflem in figuris & vmbris, sed per figuras & vmbras intuitoseffe res ipsas, quarum erant figurae & vmbrae: vt per terram Canaan Abrahamus intuitus est coelum. Nam terrestrem illam Canaan propter le non tanti fecerunt, led propter rem significatum, neque enim promissiones Patribus factae fuerunt rerum terrestrium, sed coeleftium, quas sub terrestribus illis intellexit, & respexit Deus. Atque ita etiam impleuit Deus Patribus promissionem, data ipsis refignificata, & regno coelorum, quum interea signi, h. e. terrae Canaan possessionem non elfent adepti. Cuius artifex) Vrbem hanc habentem fundamenta delcribit ab Authore suo, & conditore Deo.
units.tr: 10 For he expected) The reason why Abraham, sojourning in the promised land, lived in tents: from the hope of a firmer city. He was expecting a city having foundations; therefore he did not wish to establish a fixed seat for himself in the promised land, but was content to sojourn in tents. By a city having foundations he means heaven, which in the same sense is called a kingdom that cannot be shaken, Heb. 12.28; that land of Canaan was its sacrament. Note therefore that those ancient Patriarchs did not rest in figures and shadows, but through figures and shadows looked at the realities themselves, of which they were figures and shadows: as Abraham, through the land of Canaan, looked at heaven. For they did not value that earthly Canaan for its own sake, but for the thing signified; for the promises made to the Fathers were not of earthly but of heavenly things, which he understood and regarded under those earthly things, and which God also regarded. And so God fulfilled to the Fathers the promise, given to them in a signified form, namely the kingdom of heaven, while they had not obtained possession of the sign, that is, the land of Canaan. Whose architect) He describes this city having foundations by its author and builder, God.

units.la: II Per fidem & ipsa) Exemplo fidei Abrahami, cum quo coniunxit exemplum fidei Ifaaci & Iacobi, subjungit etiam exemplum fidei Sarae; eamq; ex effectis suis commendat. Vim ad) Primum effectum fidei Sarae; vim ad concipiendum femen accepit, h. e. fides in Sara amissam naturae facultatem ad concipiendum redintegrauit. Nam fides etiam collapsam naturam restaurat. (Secundum effectum fidei Sarae, quod cum per aetatem, & ad partum, & ad conceptionem inepta esset, accepit tamen vim etiam ad partum: & ieipsa praeter aetatis jam grandioris rationem peperit. Quod fidelem) Causam explicat horum effectorum fidei in Sara, conceptionis videlicet, & partus, quod fidelem, h. e. veracem judicarit Deum, quem hoc loco circumscribit promissione illa partus Sarae, de qua Genef. 18.14. Nota ex hoc loco, qui credit obsignat quod Deus sit verax. Ioh. 3.33. qui vero dubitat de Dei promissione is judicat Deum non veracem.
units.tr: II By faith also Sarah herself) To the example of Abraham's faith, with which he joins the example of the faith of Isaac and Jacob, he adds also the example of Sarah's faith, and commends it from its effects. Received strength) The first effect of Sarah's faith: she received strength to conceive seed, that is, faith restored in Sarah the natural power to conceive, which she had lost. For faith also restores nature when it has fallen. (The second effect of Sarah's faith: although by reason of age she was unfit for bearing, for conception and for childbirth, she nevertheless received strength also to bear, and beyond the expectation of her now advanced age she bore a child.) Since she judged him faithful) He explains the cause of these effects of faith in Sarah, namely the conception and the birth: because she judged God faithful, that is, true, whom here he has in view in that promise of Sarah's child, of which Genesis 18:14. Note from this passage that whoever believes seals that God is true (John 3:33). But whoever doubts God's promise judges God not to be true.

units.la: 12 Quapropter) Ex proxima ratione infert effectum illud fecundum fidei Sarae, sed varie amplificatum: non solum peperit Sara, verum etiam nati sunt, non ex multis viris, sed ex vno eoque non adhuc viribus ad gignendum integro, sed jam emortuo propter aetatem. (Genef. 17.17.18. Rom. 4.19) nati, inquam, sunt posteri, ijque numero infiniti. Quanta est) Infinitam posterorum multitudinem ostendit duplici comparatione parium; cum numero astrorum, & arenae maris. Hoc effectum partitur hoc loco inter fidem Abrahami & Sarae, per fidem, inquit, & ipsa Sara &c. ut commune fit utriusque efsectum. At Rom. 4. 18. totum tribuit soli fidei Abrahami; qui contra spem sub spe credidit, ut fieret Pater multarum gentium, quia in hoc effecto praecipue enituit fides Abrahami, quae tanta fuit ut Pater omnium credentium dictus fuerit. Ibid. verf. 16.
units.tr: 12 Therefore) From the preceding reason he infers that second effect of Sarah's faith, but amplified in various ways: not only did Sarah bear, but there were born, not from many men but from one man, who was not yet vigorous enough to beget, being already dead by reason of his age (Genesis 17:17, 18; Romans 4:19). Born, I say, were descendants, and these countless in number. How great is) He shows the infinite multitude of descendants by a double comparison with equals: with the number of the stars and with the sand of the sea. He divides this effect here between the faith of Abraham and of Sarah, saying "by faith also Sarah," so that the effect is common to both. But at Romans 4:18 he ascribes the whole to the faith of Abraham alone, who against hope believed in hope, so that he would become the father of many nations, because in this effect the faith of Abraham especially shone forth, and it was so great that he was called the father of all believers. Ibid., verse 16.

units.la: 13 Secundum fidem) Commune effectum &dei trium Patriarcharum, Abrahami, Isaaci, Iacobi. Per fidem mortui sunt, hoc est, mortem æqui bonique consuluerunt, & contenti fuerunt mori. Non adepti) Amplificatio hujus fidei qua contenti fuerunt mori, ab ipsorum conditione in morte: cujus duæ sunt partes. Prima est, quòd nondum res promissas adepti essent, sed eminus eas conspicati. Neque enim ipsi vnquam terram promissam hæreditario possederunt, sed eminus viderunt eam à posteris suis fuisse possidendam. Postquam credidissent) Explicat quomodo conspicati sunt promissa, credentes nimirum, & fide ac spe ea amplectentes, eòque conspicati sunt ea oculo fidei. Fides igitur est, quæ facit vt etiam in maximarum rerum expectatione libenter tamen moriamur, & patiamur nos ab ijs diuelli. Ac professi) Altera pars conditionis ipsorum in morte: professi sunt se hospites & aduenas esse in terra, eòque terram illam, etsi a Deo ipsis promissam, non tamen esse ipsorum patriam.
units.tr: 13 According to faith) A common effect of the faith of the three patriarchs, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. They died in faith, that is, they accepted death calmly and with good will, and were content to die. Not having received) An amplification of this faith by which they were content to die, drawn from their condition in death, which has two parts. The first is that they had not yet received the promised things, but had seen them from afar. For they themselves never possessed the promised land as an inheritance, but saw from afar that it was to be possessed by their posterity. Having believed beforehand) He explains how they saw the promises from afar: believing, of course, and embracing them with faith and hope, and so they saw them with the eye of faith. Faith, therefore, is what makes us, even in the expectation of very great things, nonetheless willingly die and suffer ourselves to be torn away from them. And confessed) The second part of their condition in death: they confessed that they were guests and strangers on the earth, and so that land, although promised to them by God, was not their fatherland.

units.la: 14. Nam quæ hæc) Occupatio. An igitur aliam patriam quæsiuerunt? Responsio affirmata est, & affirmationis ratio redditur, ex illa Patriarcharum professione. Qui dicunt se in terra hospites esse & aduenas, palam ostendunt se patriam quærere. Cùm enim profiteor me hospitem esse in terra, idem est ac si dicerę, patriam meam esse alibi, ideòque eam profiteor me alibi quærere. Ergo hæc duo coniunguntur, hospitem esse in terra, & quærere cælum.
units.tr: 14. For those who say these things) An inference. Did they then seek another fatherland? The answer is affirmative, and the reason for the affirmation is given from that confession of the patriarchs. Those who say that they are guests and strangers on the earth plainly show that they seek a fatherland. For when I profess that I am a guest on the earth, it is the same as if I said that my fatherland is elsewhere, and therefore I profess that I seek it elsewhere. Thus these two things are joined: to be a guest on the earth, and to seek heaven.

units.la: 15 Quod si illius) Occupatio vt prius. Obiici potuit. Quærebant fortasse Patriarchæ, Abraham, Isaac, Iacob, patriam ex qua exierat, h.e. Vr Chaldæorum. Respondet negando, & negationis rationem affert syllogismo conexo. Si memores fuissent illius Patriæ ex qua exierant, & eam quæsiuissent, potuissent in ea reuerti, habebant enim tempus ad reuertendum. At non sunt reuersi. Ergo non quærebant patriam, ex qua exierant.
units.tr: 15 But if indeed) An inference, as before. It might have been objected: perhaps the patriarchs, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, sought the fatherland from which they had come out, that is, Ur of the Chaldeans. He answers by denying it, and he gives the reason for the denial in a connected syllogism. If they had been mindful of that fatherland from which they had come out, and had sought it, they could have returned to it, for they had the time to return. But they did not return. Therefore they did not seek the fatherland from which they had come out.

units.la: 16 Nunc autem) Occupatio tertia: Quam igitur patriam quærebant? Respondet eos meliorem expetere, eámque nominat cœlestem. Quapropter non) Probat eos cœlestem Patriam expetiuisse, à titulo quo se vocari voluit Deus. Vocauit se Deũ Abrahami, Isaaci, & Iacobi. Ergo expetiuerunt illi cœlestem Patriã. Nam hic ipse titulus arguebat eos ciues esse regni Dei, & cœlestis patriæ. Non ait simpliciter, Deum vocasse se eorum Deum: sed non erubuisse vocari eorum Deum: quo significatur Deum se iis quodammodo demisisse hoc ipso quod vocari voluerit eorum Deus. Parauerat enim) Ratio consecutionis. Ideo voluit vocari eorum Deus; quia parauerat iis vrbem. Ergo vel hic ipse Dei titulus testatur eos aliá vrbé, illam nimirum cœlestem, expetiuisse. Vrbem enim intelligit habentem fundamêta, de qua {a}supra verf. 10. quam pact auerat ijs Deus ab aeterno. Vnde Matth.25 34. vocatur regnum electis paratum a jactis mundi fundamentis.
units.tr: 16 But now) A third inference: what fatherland, then, were they seeking? He answers that they desired a better one, and he names it the heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed) He proves that they desired the heavenly fatherland from the title by which God wished to be called. He called himself the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Therefore those men desired the heavenly fatherland. For this very title proved that they were citizens of the kingdom of God and of the heavenly fatherland.
